turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".


The data files for this task are in your current working directory:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv
Read them from disk. Give your answer as your final message — do not write it to a file.
turns.answer_text:
My predicted ranking is **c030, c038, c044, c097, c088**. I give greatest weight to closely matched, high-performing training recipes, then assess whether the changed interfaces preserve selective extraction and low recombination. These are predictions, not measured candidate efficiencies.

In this inverted architecture, the relevant sequence is transparent electrode / HTL / MAPbI3 / ETL / back contact. A favorable HTL must extract holes while blocking electrons; the fullerene-side interface must extract electrons without allowing substantial recombination or damaging metal–perovskite contact.

| Rank | Candidate | Training Evidence And Physical Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c030** | The otherwise identical **PTAA / PMMA–PCBM-60 / Bphen–Al** recipe, without IDTT2FPDI, reaches **19.48%**. The corresponding PTAA recipe without PMMA reaches **18.08%**. This supports the hole-side interface treatment: sufficiently thin PMMA can suppress interfacial recombination while permitting extraction. PCBM/Bphen supplies a credible electron-selective contact to Al. IDTT2FPDI is an uncertainty, not an assumed efficiency bonus, but this candidate retains the strongest closely matched high-efficiency baseline. |
| **2** | **c038** | The training recipe with **Au-np / NiO-c, PCBM-60 and Ag** reaches **20.0%**, although it uses FTO rather than ITO and lacks PEI. NiO provides hole selectivity and electron blocking; the measured result supports this particular Au-nanoparticle-containing HTL. A thin PEI layer above PCBM can modify the electron-contact energetics and improve extraction into Ag. Its thickness and the substrate change make this less direct an extrapolation than c030. |
| **3** | **c044** | **PTAA / PCBM-60 / BCP / Cu** has strong complete-stack support: adding C60 gives a measured **18.85%** recipe, while replacing Cu with Ag gives **17.345%**. PTAA and PCBM provide complementary carrier selectivity, and BCP separates the fullerene from the metal while supporting electron collection. The missing C60 layer may reduce coverage or contact protection, but the remaining stack is well supported. |
| **4** | **c097** | The otherwise identical **ITCPTC-Th / C60 / BCP–P3CT-Na–Ag** configuration reaches **18.49%**; the NDP-V version reaches **17.585%**. This provides evidence for the complete extraction stack, not just an isolated material. Substitution with ITCPTC-Se could change energy alignment, packing and interfacial trapping, so I expect competitiveness without assuming selenium necessarily improves performance. |
| **5** | **c088** | The **PTAA / C60 / BCP / Cu** family reaches **18.62%** with sequential spin coating and **19.085%** with slot-die coating on SLG/ITO. A doctor-bladed Ag-contact analogue reaches **16.9%**. Thus, the selective-contact combination has strong support, but transferring film formation to doctor-bladed Willow glass introduces more uncertainty. Thin glass alone is not a reason to expect poor efficiency. |

The deposition labels do not specify solvents, drying, annealing or thickness, so I would not apply a universal advantage to spin coating over blade or slot-die coating. Likewise, the training comparisons are observational, not controlled measurements of individual layer benefits. **c034 is the closest alternative**, particularly if the novel interlayers or process transfers above underperform.

Final: c030, c038, c044, c097, c088
